data.title: Genuine Material Distorted to Carry the Claim
data.summary:
The campaign's central claim is built on genuine material — a real document, statistic or
quotation — presented without the context that changes its meaning.
data.description:
This is the most durable construction available to an operator, because every element is
verifiable. Fact-checking confirms the source, the quotation and the number, and
confirmation is what the audience takes away. The distortion lives in framing, which
fact-checking does not address.

A kernel of truth also protects the campaign against takedown: platforms are reluctant to
act on content that is technically accurate, and the organisation's own rebuttal must
begin by conceding the facts.

The analytic task is to state precisely what was removed — the sentence before the
quotation, the denominator under the statistic, the date. That specificity is what makes
the finding usable; "taken out of context" without the missing context is not a finding.
data.recommendation:
* Respond by supplying the missing context in full rather than by disputing the facts,
  which are correct.
* Publish the complete source material where possible, so the context is available
  without the organisation having to narrate it.
* Expect platform reporting to fail on this content and plan the response accordingly.
data.short_recommendation: Supply the missing context; do not dispute the verifiable facts.
